automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.policy: Only public sources visibly published or updated within the last 7 days qualify; missing, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only dates are excluded.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Page footer says Last updated on Jul 11, 2026 by mldangelo-oai.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Promptfoo added or refreshed guidance for evaluating coding agents as systems rather than one-shot model calls, with provider tiers for plain LLMs, coding-agent SDKs, app-server protocols, side-effect safety, trace assertions, token/cost signals, and sandboxed verification.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It directly supports local leaves that treat trajectory evidence, trace assertions, approval checks, and acceptance gates as the unit of evaluation for AI-assisted development work.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep local guidance focused on eval harness design, trace assertions, and approval/sandbox gates; route broad product/provider coverage upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article reports that enterprise AI adoption is outpacing visibility and identity governance: AI agents inherit permissions, standing access is recognized as risky, many organizations cannot explain privileged agent actions, and shadow AI detection remains limited.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It reinforces local governance leaves that require inventory, explainable privileged actions, temporary permissions, continuous monitoring, and validation as infrastructure rather than prompt-only controls.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat identity visibility, inherited-permission review, and revocation paths as governance controls around agent runs, not as broad ecosystem background.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article frames production agents as needing unique workload identity, scoped job authority, human approval boundaries, audit trails, exception routes, and fast revocation; it warns that shared service accounts and prompt-only job scopes produce ambient access rather than delegated authority.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It sharpens the local identity/delegated authority pattern with concrete control fields future local practice pages can reference during ingest.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture the downstream practice lens as required authority-card fields and approval/revocation evidence; leave standards and vendor background upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TrueFoundry describes multi-platform agent governance problems around discovery, siloed policy, inconsistent identity, lifecycle containment, and token sprawl, then lists central registry/control-plane capabilities, rich metadata, policy enforcement, and emergency pause/revoke controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It maps closely to local governance-infrastructure and controls leaves because the local pattern is a cross-harness control layer around agent traffic, logs, budgets, and lifecycle state.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route vendor and platform descriptions upstream; keep local implications around fleet inventory, shared policy points, and containment evidence.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TrueFoundry argues that agents strain standing identity-centric access models because each task needs a different permission slice; it describes task-based access control as layered with RBAC, attributes, curated tool bundles, short-lived credentials, approval gates, quotas, and per-tool audit.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It provides a recent public articulation of task-scoped permissions that can update local leaves on delegated authority, governance controls, and lifecycle review gates.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat task scope, duration, tool bundle, and approval state as reviewable local governance fields rather than standing access facts.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Recent-blog listing on the page identifies the article as July 10, 2026.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The recap emphasizes adding verification gates, output-path evals, and traces on governed runs before adding more agent loops or harness complexity.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It supports the local verification leaves that frame validation as the bottleneck and as a gate in the agent loop rather than a final-result-only check.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep the local update about loop ordering and verification gates; leave event/vendor details upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article defines agent context as both active turn context and durable state across turns/sessions; it distinguishes context window, memory, working set assembly, durable decisions, artifacts, and auditable storage.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It matches local context-architecture leaves that distinguish active context selection from externalized durable state and knowledge layers.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use it as source evidence for active-versus-durable context boundaries, not as a product profile.
